title: Phased decommissioning runbook with pin-preservation & published performance profiles
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Create an operational runbook and automation suite for decommissioning old model versions while preserving customer pin behavior and publishing a stable performance profile snapshot. This ticket covers the end-to-end workflow: deprecation triggers, public notices, migration guides, console + API UI affordances, SDK warnings, automated compatibility checks, and monitoring/dashboards for regressions. The goal is to ensure customers can safely pin older versions without unexpected service loss, get clear migration paths, and see published performance tradeoffs to choose alternatives.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook doc published in Confluence with step-by-step decommissioning checklist and escalation paths
Console: model page shows deprecation banner with timeline and link to migration guide
Automated email templates and in-console notices at 90/60/30/14/7/0 days pre-deprecation are created and tested
SDK and HTTP API return deprecation warnings when a pinned model is older than the published EOL threshold with suggested replacement model IDs
Performance profile snapshot for the deprecated version published in the Model Catalog (latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, quality eval summaries)
Compatibility checker runs in staging for a representative set of prompts and flags any >5% quality regression against recommended replacement
Support runbook & escalation Slack channel created and staff trained for first two decomm events
At least one Canary customer migration performed end-to-end and documented with lessons learned
